2027-03-13.title: Saturday of the fifth week of the Great Fast
readings: The field and cave of Machpelah become Abraham's; Sarah is buried
Boasting excluded; justified by faith; we uphold the law
You are my friends; I chose you
2027-03-13.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), fifth week. Anniversary of the episcopal ordination (2010) of the Most Rev. Vincent Mar Paulos, Thomas Mar Antonios, Samuel Mar Irenios and Philipose Mar Stephanos. Tomorrow is Samio Sunday, the Sunday of the healing of the blind man.
2027-03-13.verse: No one has greater love than this, to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.
theo: The story of the field at Hebron ends with a legal formula repeated twice: “So the field of Ephron in Machpelah… the field with the cave that was in it and all the trees that were in the field… passed to Abraham as a possession.” Then, simply: “After this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah facing Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.” The first part of the promised land that Abraham owns is a tomb. Later Abraham himself will be laid there, and Isaac and Rebekah, and Jacob and Leah. It looks like a sad ending, but it is an act of hope. To bury your dead in the land of promise is to say: God will keep his word, even beyond death. The Letter to the Hebrews says of the patriarchs: “they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God.” Christian cemeteries carry the same faith; we call them places of sleep, because we await the resurrection of the body.

St Paul asks: “Then what becomes of boasting? It is excluded. By what law? By that of works? No, but by the law of faith. For we hold that a person is justified by faith apart from works prescribed by the law.” Abraham did not earn the promise; he received it and trusted it, even to the grave. Paul means that no one is made righteous by the observances of the Mosaic law, and the Church teaches that justification is God's free gift, received in faith and baptism, which then bears fruit in love; so no one can boast. And Paul adds at once: “Is he not the God of Gentiles also? Yes… since God is one,” and “Do we then overthrow the law by this faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the law.” The law is fulfilled in the commandment Jesus gives in the Gospel: “This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. No one has greater love than this, to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.” He calls us friends, not servants, and he reminds us whose initiative it was: “You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last.” St Augustine commented that Christ did not choose us because we were good; he chose us so that we might become good (in substance). Today we give thanks for four shepherds of our Church, Vincent Mar Paulos, Thomas Mar Antonios, Samuel Mar Irenios and Philipose Mar Stephanos, ordained bishops on this day in 2010: chosen and appointed to bear fruit that will last. Tomorrow, on Samio Sunday, the Lord opens the eyes of the blind.
outline: Ask: what is my hope built on?
Point 1 · A tomb in the land of promise
Justified by faith, the law upheld.
Friends who lay down their lives and bear fruit.
“No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends.”
live: Pray this week at the grave of someone you love, or light a candle at home, and say the Creed slowly, especially “the resurrection of the body.”
Do one hidden act of self-giving today for someone who cannot repay you.
2027-03-13.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you laid down your life for your friends and called us friends, not servants. You chose us, not because we were good, but so that we might become good and bear fruit that will last. Exclude all boasting from our hearts, keep us in the faith of Abraham who buried his dead in hope, and bless our bishops Vincent Mar Paulos, Thomas Mar Antonios, Samuel Mar Irenios and Philipose Mar Stephanos, whom you chose and appointed for your people. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Friend who laid down his life for us gives us his Body and Blood, so that we may love one another as he has loved us.

quick: The field and cave of Machpelah became Abraham's possession, and there he buried Sarah in the land of promise.
Boasting is excluded: we are justified by faith, and the law is upheld, not overthrown.
Jesus calls us friends, chose us, and appointed us to bear fruit that will last.
2027-03-13.action: Do one hidden act of love for someone who cannot repay you.
2027-03-13.question: Do I live as one chosen and loved by Christ, or as one trying to earn his love?

family.explain: Jesus says: I do not call you servants, I call you friends. He chose each of us. The greatest love is to give your life for your friends, and that is what Jesus did on the Cross. Today we also pray for four of our bishops, whom Jesus chose to be shepherds of our Church.
family.intention: We pray for our bishops and for all who serve the Church.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show Jesus' kind of love to someone this week?”

illus: A schoolteacher in Thiruvalla kept a small card on her desk for thirty years. Her first headmistress had given it to her on her first day. It said only: you did not choose these children; they were given to you. On difficult days, when a class was noisy or a child seemed hopeless, she would turn the card over in her fingers. At her retirement a former student, now a doctor, stood up to speak and said: she treated each of us as if we had been chosen. Then he held up the same kind of card. She had given one to every student who had ever thanked her.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us your friends. Teach us to love one another as you have loved us. Amen.
share: Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah (Genesis 23:19). What does my faith say to me at the grave?
Then what becomes of boasting? It is excluded (Romans 3:27). Where do I still try to earn God's love?
You did not choose me but I chose you (John 15:16). How does it change me to know that Christ chose me?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your love.
interc: For Vincent Mar Paulos, Thomas Mar Antonios, Samuel Mar Irenios and Philipose Mar Stephanos, on the anniversary of their episcopal ordination.
For all bishops, that they may lay down their lives for their flocks.
For those who think they must earn God's love.
For friendships that are faithful and holy.
For our parish as we approach Samio Sunday and the last weeks of the Fast.
pm.close: Father, your Son called us friends and chose us to bear fruit that will last. Keep us humble in faith, generous in love, and faithful in hope until we see the city you have prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the field and the cave of Machpelah passed to Abraham, and Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah (Genesis 23:19). His first possession in the promised land was a grave. To bury his dead there was an act of hope.

Paul asks: then what becomes of boasting? It is excluded. For we hold that a person is justified by faith apart from works prescribed by the law (Romans 3:27–28). Abraham received the promise as a gift; so do we. And yet faith does not overthrow the law: we uphold the law (Romans 3:31).

Jesus sums up the law: this is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends (John 15:12–13). He calls us friends.

And he says: you did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last (John 15:16). Today we thank God for our four bishops ordained on this day in 2010, and we ask that each of us may bear fruit that lasts. Tomorrow the Lord opens the eyes of the blind; may he open ours. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: I call you my friends, and I chose you! Isn't that wonderful? Jesus loved us so much that he gave his life for us on the Cross. Today we pray for four of our bishops whom Jesus chose. This week, be a good friend to someone who is lonely.

intro: Theme: “No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends.”
A tomb in the land of promise, a faith that excludes boasting, and the Friend who chose us to bear fruit that will last.

points.h: A tomb in the land of promise
sub: The field and the cave of Machpelah.
q: For I know that my Redeemer lives, and that at the last he will stand upon the earth;
But as it is, they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God; indeed, he has prepared a city for them.
points.apply: Pray the Creed slowly this week, dwelling on the resurrection of the body.

sub: The God of Jews and Gentiles.
q: Thus says the Lord: Do not let the wise boast in their wisdom, do not let the mighty boast in their might, do not let the wealthy boast in their wealth;
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one grace you did nothing to deserve.

q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
We love because he first loved us.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for your bishop and do one hidden act of self-giving love.

concl: Abraham buried his dead in hope; Christ has opened the tomb.
Chosen as friends, we are sent to love as he loved and to bear lasting fruit.
2027-03-13.resolve: Live the last weeks of the Fast as Christ's chosen friends, humble in faith and generous in love.
